text:
### Observed differences

- **Participation halved for six activities.** Before, A33, A35, A36, A37, A38 and A39 each appeared in every trace (100 in 100, at most once per case); in the later window each appears in only about 47–57 in 100 traces (A33, A35, A36 about 47; A37, A38, A39 about 56–57). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]

- **From "always both trios" to "one of two trios".** Before, the trio A33/A35/A36 and the trio A37/A38/A39 always shared traces, with the first trio before the second in about 99–100 in 100 traces. In the later window, traces containing activities from both trios drop to about 2–4 in 100: about 44 in 100 later traces contain only the first trio and about 53 in 100 only the second, while cases with neither trio are essentially absent. [REL001, REL004, REL015, REL017, REL019, REL021, REL022, REL024]

- **Within-trio behaviour unchanged.** In both windows each trio's members still occur together and in no fixed order (A33 and A35 run in both orders in roughly equal shares before and after), and they are skipped together — in about 53 in 100 later traces neither A33 nor A35 appears. [REL013, REL014, REL018, REL025, REL026, REL027]

- **Bracketing activities unchanged.** A30 and A31 still occur in every trace in both windows; A30 still precedes the first trio whenever it runs, and the second trio still precedes A31. [REL001, REL004, REL007, REL010]

- **New direct edges at the block's boundaries.** Before, A30's outgoing transitions led only into the first trio (A33 about 34%, A35 about 36%, A36 about 29% of them); in the later window about 53 in 100 lead directly into the second trio. Conversely, the first-trio activities now flow directly to A31 (about 33 in 100 of A33's, 34 in 100 of A35's and 24 in 100 of A36's outgoing transitions), which was not observed before. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the six-activity block between A30 and A31 — previously executed in full in every case as the unordered trio A33/A35/A36 followed by the unordered trio A37/A38/A39 — became an exclusive choice: in the later window almost every case runs exactly one of the two trios, about 47 in 100 only A33/A35/A36 and about 53 in 100 only A37/A38/A39, with both trios together in only about 3 in 100 cases. This is a structural change rather than a re-weighting of existing paths, because the cross-trio co-occurrence and the direct boundary edges are present in one window and (nearly) absent in the other. The signs are direct and mutually consistent: participation of all six activities fell from 100% to roughly half [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]; cross-trio co-occurrence collapsed from 100% to about 2–4 in 100 [REL015, REL019, REL022]; within-trio co-occurrence and mixed internal order persisted [REL013, REL025]; A30 and A31 still bracket the block [REL001, REL007]; and the new edges appear exactly where the skipped trio used to sit [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]. Every item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled data, and 45 control-flow items qualified against fewer than 1 expected without change, so the pattern as a whole is not what a stable process produces.

Limitations: the evidence shows which edges changed but not how the choice between the trios is made — no deciding activity or condition is visible in these indicators — and it does not explain the small residue of later cases (about 3 in 100) that still contain both trios; the roughly 47/53 split also rests on single samples of 200 traces per window. [REL015, DIR001]

Other differences: event positions shifted slightly in the direction the structural change predicts — A30 sits later (median about 0.63 to 0.69 of the trace), the first trio later (about 0.69 to 0.73–0.75), and A31 and the second trio slightly earlier — consistent with shorter average cases when only one trio runs; these are event-position shifts, not clock-time moves, and are by-products of the main change rather than independent confirmation. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]
